subject: 16k context: sudden p95/p99 latency spikes affecting production
messages:
From: Audrey Nguyen <audrey.nguyen@clearpath.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: support@clearpath.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: increased latencies for long-context batches

Hi Vivek / Neha,

We're seeing repeated p95/p99 spikes in our production jobs when clients hit ~16k token context windows. The 95th is moving from ~200ms to ~1.2s on some routes, and p99s are spiking to 3-4s intermittently. This started after we increased context size for a subset of enterprise users last week.

Attached is a small sample of requests + timings (clearpath_latency_sample_16k.json). We also noticed a higher error-rate (429s and occasional 503s) when concurrent long-context streams increase. This is affecting two of our tier-1 customers and they want an ETA. Can you triage?

Thanks,
Audrey
Audrey Nguyen
Platform Ops, ClearPath AI

--

Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: increased latencies for long-context batches

Hi Audrey — thanks for the sample and the heads up. We're escalating internally and I'll own coordination.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share the model name + exact tokenization settings for the 16k workload?
- Are those requests single-stream (one large prompt) or multi-chunked by the client?

Marissa (CS) — please join for customer communication. Marcus / Eng (cc'd) — I'll send traces and schedule a deep-dive first thing Monday. We want to know if this is a serving runtime regression, a kernel fallback, or queueing caused by batching.

I'll follow up with an interim mitigation plan within 24 hours.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: URGENT: ClearPath AI p95/p99 spikes on 16k context — need triage

Team — looping you in. Customer reported large regressions over weekend. They included a sample and noted 429/503 errors when concurrent long-context load rises.

Key facts:
- Affects hosted API routes for ClearPath AI (multi-tenant hosted).
- Spike correlates with requests ~14-17k tokens.
- Symptoms: p95 from ~200ms -> ~1.2s, p99 3-4s, occasional 429/503.
- Started after last Friday's model profile update (we rolled new kernel selection heuristics).

Immediate requests:
1) Marcus — can you pull serving traces for the tenant during the time window 2026-12-12 22:00 to 2026-12-13 02:00 UTC? Check KV cache hits, kernel fallback counts, and queue lengths.
2) Eng — throttle suggestions: can we reduce per-tenant max concurrent long-context batches as a short-term control?
3) Marissa/Neha — prepare a one-paragraph customer-safe summary.

I'll set a 9:00am PT sync to go over findings. If this looks like a regression from the kernel heuristics we may need exec attention for a rollback.

-V
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:13:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: ClearPath AI p95/p99 spikes on 16k context — need triage

Quick update from initial triage (I pulled traces + traces bundle attached: redwood_server_traces_20261214.zip):
- We see a pattern where large-context requests frequently fall back to a slower kernel path for mid-sequence attention because the kernel selector chose a quantized fallback for memory reasons. Fallbacks correspond with the p99 tail.
- There are periodic queue buildups on the multi-tenant pool when several 16k requests arrive simultaneously; batching heuristics were combining windows causing oversized batch execution which increased tail latency.
- KV cache hit rates are slightly lower for this tenant due to their prompt patterns (lots of unique prefixes), so caching saved less CPU than expected.

Short-term mitigations I recommend:
A) Patch runtime to prefer the faster kernel for sequences under 18k when memory headroom is borderline (hotfix),
B) Enforce per-tenant concurrent long-context cap (example: max 6 concurrent 16k streams),
C) Add a request-level soft-fail that suggests chunking when we detect >12k tokens + high concurrent load.

I'll prepare a short rollback plan for the kernel selector change we rolled last Friday in case we need to revert. If exec signs off, we can deploy hotfix A within 6-8 hours and B within 2 hours (config change).

-Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: increased latencies for long-context batches

Hi Audrey — quick update for your leadership and customers:

We identified a likely cause and have three mitigations ready. We're recommending a staged approach: apply a configuration limit on concurrent long-context streams for your tenant immediately to prevent further p99 spikes, and simultaneously deploy a hotfix to prefer the faster kernel when safe.

Planned timeline (estimates):
- Now (within 30m): Apply temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for 16k contexts (protects other customers too).
- 6-8 hours: Hotfix to avoid the slower kernel fallback for this workload (Marcus will lead).
- 24-48 hours: Monitor and, if stable, roll the change broadly or revert kernel selector if any regression.

We will confirm once the cap is applied and share a short post-mortem with sample traces. Would you like a call with eng (Marcus) this afternoon to walk through technical details for ClearPath's platform team?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Audrey Nguyen <audrey.nguyen@clearpath.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearpath.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 18:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: increased latencies for long-context batches — interim controls applied

Audrey / Daniel —

Thanks for your patience. Summary of actions taken and next steps: 

What we changed (interim):
- Applied a per-tenant concurrency cap of 6 for 16k-context requests to prevent queue amplification (took effect 2026-12-14 13:30 PT).
- Deployed kernel-selection hotfix to prefer the faster path for sequences up to 18k when memory headroom is near threshold (deployed 2026-12-14 18:02 PT).

Early results:
- Customer metrics: p95 reduced from 1.2s to ~280ms within the protected window; p99s dropped under 1.1s in our test window. Error rates for 429/503 fell back to baseline. We will continue 72-hour monitoring and share dashboards.

Follow-ups:
- Marcus will produce a short post-mortem and a safe roll-forward plan by Friday (2026-12-18).
- Marissa/Neha will schedule a debrief call for ClearPath leadership tomorrow to review the mitigation and long-term options (model quantization profiles, dedicated pool, or prompt-chunking recommendations).

If you'd like us to provision dedicated capacity or help change client-side chunking quickly, we can fast-track that conversation. Thanks again for raising this early — we aim to keep your production SLAs solid.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
